answer: An applicant completes a one-way voyage whose five waypoints are drawn from a published atlas by hashing the applicant key with the epoch seed. At each waypoint a distinct keeper extends a vine credential by signing a live challenge that includes the prior graft; the vine cannot be forked or handed off. If applicants share two keepers, recycle a vine root, or present matching live-task preimage patterns, the protocol slashes their voyage deposits and sequesters those keepers for two epochs, so cloned identities cannot cheaply reuse one operator ring.
